0.original: Y'shtola seems eager to share your discoveries with the others.

48.original: Thank you for assisting me with my investigations. I shall seek out our companions and share what we have learned.

49.original: ...Much as I would like to tell you to sit down and leave the rest to us, your condition demands that we make all reasonable haste.

50.original: If you are not too weary, it may be useful to speak with Paushs Ooan again, and ask if there is aught else he is willing to divulge.

51.original: Ah, Alphinaud's friend. You and your companions have done much to repair the damage caused when the waters parted...

52.original: ...Anything elssse you can do? Hmmm... Have you been to the Walls of the Forgotten?

54.original: I...think I've just come from them.

55.original: Are they the ruins to the northwest?

56.original: The remnants to the northwest, yesss? You visited them unbidden? Pshhh... Could it be that your footsteps were guided by the ancientsss...?

57.original: Yesss, that is the sacred site of which I ssspeak. Could it be that your footsssteps were guided there by the ancientsss...?

58.original: I believe it may be ssso. Listen then, and I will tell you of our plans to bring light to the Walls, that we might answer the shining call of the illuminated land.

59.original: We have requested a finless craftsman to shape for us a sssacred lamp. He is odd for a land-dweller, choosing as he does to live in the ocean, but his ssskill is beyond question.

60.original: It is concerning, however, that we have heard nothing of his progress. If you were to visit this artisan and return with our long-awaited light, then any doubt as to your purpossse would be laid to ressst.

61.original: His name is “Grenoldt.” You will find his workshop in a metal structure to the sssouth.

62.original: Go, visit Grenoldt in his “Workbench.” Bring back the lamp we asssked for, and all will be as the ancients desired.

63.original: Oh, that's just <hex:021A020203>great<hex:021A020103>, that is. Me mind's playin' tricks on me now. “Look, Grenoldt! Someone's come to visit ye <hex:021A020203>at the bottom o' the bleedin' ocean<hex:021A020103>!”

64.original: Or might be as yer a ghost, eh? Go on, foul shade, feast yerself on me rotten soul...

65.original: I've got no use for it. A craftsman what can't craft is more pointless than a sea slug with a domin' hammer. An' that's an insult to bloody sea slugs...

66.original: Grenoldt appears to be suffering from a crushing bout of self-doubt. Maybe you can help <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>psych<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> him up.

68.original: Grenoldt appears to be suffering from a crushing bout of self-doubt. Maybe you can help <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>psych<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> him up.

69.original: What is it ye want, specter? If yer not here to end me misery, then bugger off back to damnation...

70.original: ...Eh? Ye wouldn't be tryin' to raise me spirits now, would ye, spirit? Not what ye'd expect from a servant o' the netherworld...

72.original: Has it really come to this...?

76.original: ...What's that supposed to mean? Not impressed with what ye see, <hex:02080EE905FF056C617373FF046C616403>?

77.original: Aye, well...I may have let meself go a bit. This was meant to be me underwater sanctuary─a place where I could concentrate on me work, far from the distractions o' the outside world...

78.original: Er... Might be as we crossed paths back in the Crystarium, but I don't reckon we've been formally introduced.

79.original: Name's Grenoldt. An' this here's meant to be me underwater sanctuary─a place where I can give meself over to me work, far from the distractions o' the outside world...

80.original: Aye. Though I wonder how ye bloody well found me...

81.original: This here's meant to be me underwater sanctuary─a place where I can give meself over to me work, far from the distractions o' the outside world...

82.original: ...An' yet, here ye stand. Now what's so damned important that ye'd dive all the way down to the bottom o' the bleedin' Tempest to bother me?

84.original: Gods curse me empty head! I've not so much as made a start!

85.original: I'm worth less than a sea slug... Nay, the <hex:021A020203>slime<hex:021A020103> left by a sea slug. Me delivery date's long past, me workbench is untouched... An' I call meself a bleedin' artisan!

86.original: Ye've heard their beliefs, have ye? Bringin' light to them ruins'll be an act of <hex:021A020203>deep religious an' cultural significance<hex:021A020103>!

87.original: An' it was my privilege as a craftsman to be tasked with providin' a ritual instrument worthy o' the occasion. But I just...can't...bloody well...

88.original: GAAAH! Me mind's a bleedin' blank! It's like I've pissed away me last drop of inspiration!

89.original: Tell me ye've got summat to show me─summat as'll give me muse a right good kick up the arse...?

90.original: The Ondo want to honor the comin' o' these ancients, so their answerin' light's got to blaze with the right kind o' brightness.

91.original: Like...like the spark o' life caught in a crystal. But just bein' sparkly's not enough─it's got to dance with joy an' sorrow an' a sense o' hardship endured... Ye know what I mean!?

92.original: Your thoughts turn to the Warriors of Light from the First, and the crystals you discovered at the end of their journeys. Maybe Grenoldt would find them inspiring...

93.original: Your thoughts turn to Branden, and the crystal you discovered at the end of his journey. Maybe Grenoldt could find inspiration in that...

94.original: Your thoughts turn to Lamitt, and the crystal you discovered at the end of her journey. Maybe Grenoldt could find inspiration in that...

95.original: Your thoughts turn to Renda-Rae, and the crystal you discovered at the end of her journey. Maybe Grenoldt could find inspiration in that...

96.original: Your thoughts turn to Nyelbert, and the crystal you discovered at the end of his journey. Maybe Grenoldt could find inspiration in that...

97.original: Grenoldt seeks a particular kind of inspiration─the kind that crystallizes only at the culmination of a long and tragic tale.

98.original: Complete any of the role quest lines available at the Wandering Stairs in the Crystarium, then return to Grenoldt once more.

99.original: It's no good...<hex:02100103>I need summat <hex:021A020203>special<hex:021A020103> to light a fire under me piss-sodden imagination.

100.original: Like...like the spark o' life caught in a crystal. But just bein' sparkly's not enough─it's got to dance with joy an' sorrow an' a sense o' hardship endured... Ye know what I mean!?

101.original: Grenoldt seeks a particular kind of inspiration─the kind that crystallizes only at the culmination of a long and tragic tale.

102.original: Complete any of the role quest lines available at the Wandering Stairs in the Crystarium, then return to Grenoldt once more.

103.original: I've let the Ondo down, aye... But more'n that I've let <hex:021A020203>meself<hex:021A020103> down. Might as well go back to mendin' kettles...

104.original: Show Grenoldt a crystal which once belonged to one of Ardbert's companions?

106.original: Such strikin' beauty... It shines with heartache an' laughter an' the transience o' life, like the turmoil o' history made manifest!

107.original: Aye, I can see the brilliance o' the crystal's legacy! Ahhh...ye'd never capture such a gleam, not if ye labored a hundred years...

108.original: But bugger me if I don't mean to try! Where're me tools, gods damn ye!? I must set to work before the feelin' fades!
